title: Use-after-free in `save_picklebuffer` via re-entrant `buffer_callback` and `__bool__`
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free in a 4097-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 4097-byte region, over the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

spatial.oracle: a revoked-capability fault (cause 24) at the stale access: the object is a system allocator block and the base arm enforces revocation on its free. A bounds fault or completion would falsify this. The fault must carry cause 5, 7 or 24; any other cause, cause 2 (ILLEGAL_INST) among them, is an ordinary trap rather than this arm's mechanism and falsifies this.
spatial.oracle_premise: Corrected at review, 2026-10-10: the premise that this arm revokes is false. Its level0 heap only marks a freed block free (capstone/ports/musl-capstone/runtime/level0.c, l0_free), patch 0009 issues no revoke, and the runtime's only revoke sites release thread context areas, reached only through __clone; so nothing on this arm revokes heap memory. A cause 24 here is UNEXP_OP_TYPE, an access through an untagged base register: a pointer slot that later data overwrote (tag integrity), or an integer or NULL used as a pointer -- not revocation. The oracle above is kept as written; see results/20261006/README.md, 'Corrections made at review'.

sublet.oracle: fault: the object is a libc malloc block

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion is admissible and is the expected outcome under this guest's configuration: the run records security.cheri.runtime_revocation_every_free_default as 0 and runtime_revocation_async as 1, so revocation is sweep-based and asynchronous, and a stale access reached before the next sweep still holds a tagged capability. Where a sweep has run first the access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). A bounds fault would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial SILENT (spatial-20261006-105111); sublet DETECTED cause=24 (sublet-20261006-112658); cheribsd-revocation SILENT (cheri11)
